functionality.rationale: Durable checkpoints must preserve only verified offsets and reopen without corrupting destination state.

security.rationale: Persisted state must bind peer, transfer, manifest, destination identity, expiry, and integrity without trusting caller input.

performance.rationale: Checkpoint frequency and retained metadata bytes must remain bounded without dominating transfer throughput.

compatibility.rationale: The versioned resume schema needs an explicit migration and incompatible-state policy.

concurrency.rationale: Checkpoint writes, cleanup, replacement, and process interruption race within durable storage.

platform.rationale: Atomic metadata persistence and destination identity must behave across supported filesystems and process models.

persistence.rationale: This task defines durable, integrity-protected, bounded resume records and their cleanup.

adr.rationale: Resume introduces a durable persisted schema, migration, integrity, and retention policy.

architecture.rationale: Persistent resume state remains within the existing storage boundary; XT-073 owns session and transfer recovery.

roadmap.rationale: XT-039 owns roadmap closure after adapters, UI, and restart evidence.
